notes: BDB lists qal in three senses: (1) "go free, be unrestrained" (2) of overhanging stuffs, i.e. overrunning/exceeding/extended beyond limits. The corpus's own qal attestations (Ezek.17.6 "spreading" vine branches, Exod.26.12-13 the tabernacle curtain that "overhangs," Amos.6.4/6.7 those "sprawled" on their couches) all illustrate sense (2) only. Requested gloss "go free" was dropped: it has no citable verse in this dataset distinct from the overhang/sprawl sense, even though it's BDB's own primary listed sense for the root.

Niphal has a single, textually contested attestation (Jer.49.7, נִסְרְחָה, of Edom's wisdom). BDB itself glosses it with a question mark: "is their wisdom let loose (i.e. dismissed, gone)?; but is corrupt" -- offering two competing readings. The gloss "be let loose; be dismissed" quotes BDB's primary offered reading verbatim; flagging as single-attestation/contested per usual practice.

Niphal's sole citation (Jer.49.7, "has their wisdom vanished?") doesn't clearly match either "be let loose" or "be dismissed" -- kept the closer of the two ("be dismissed", as in wisdom having departed) but flagging as genuinely uncertain given the single, debated citation.
